chunks: From him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother, from his father Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who sets out on a journey that is a day's travel. He said: 'It is obligatory upon him to perform Qasr (shortened) prayer if it is a day's travel, even if he is engaged in his work.'

key_terms.يَدُورُ فِي عَمَلِهِ: Engaged in his work/traveling while working

ai.seo_question: When is shortened prayer obligatory for a traveler engaged in work?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the obligation of Qasr prayer is triggered by the distance of a day's travel, irrespective of the traveler's activity level. It addresses the scholarly debate on whether continuous movement or specific travel conditions are required, affirming that mere travel status suffices. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining when the concession of shortened prayers applies during journeys.
